stair-treads/sarasota.title: Stair Tread Installation Sarasota FL | Historic & Modern
stair-treads/sarasota.description: Stair tread replacement and refinishing in Sarasota, FL: Laurel Park heart-pine restoration, Gulf Gate builder-stair conversions, and 2026 installed pricing.
stair-treads/sarasota.h1: Stair Treads in Sarasota: From Laurel Park to Gulf Gate
stair-treads/sarasota.lede: Sarasota's stair work splits along the city's building eras: original heart-pine in the historic core, carpeted builder stairs everywhere the 1970s and 1980s reached.
stair-treads/sarasota.capsule: Sarasota's stair jobs split between refinishing original heart-pine treads in Laurel Park and Southside Village two-story bungalows and replacing carpeted builder stairs in 1970s-90s Gulf Gate and Meadows-area homes. A full thirteen-tread solid hardwood replacement runs $2,015-$3,705 installed in 2026; refinishing an existing staircase costs less.
stair-treads/sarasota.body_html:
Sarasota's downtown condo towers don't have stairs worth discussing here. Nearly every unit sits on a single level and is reached by elevator, so stair tread work in this city is really about the houses, not the towers. See our Sarasota area page for the rest of the city's housing profile.

Two very different staircases show up on our schedule. The first is original heart-pine or oak treads in a 1920s-1950s two-story bungalow around Laurel Park or Southside Village, usually worn through the finish in the center of each tread from decades of foot traffic. Those get sanded and re-stained in place more often than replaced outright, because the wood is typically sound underneath the wear pattern, and matching a century-old species profile with new material is harder than saving what's already there. We offer full stair refinishing alongside the tread work.

The second is a 1970s-90s two-story model in Gulf Gate or The Meadows with carpeted builder stairs over a plywood or pine stringer set. Those runs are typically twelve to fourteen treads for a standard eight-foot ceiling height, and the carpet is almost always original or a single replacement from decades back. Pulling it reveals unfinished pine treads that were never meant to be seen, usable as a base for a new tread material but not attractive enough to leave exposed. A two-story 1985 Gulf Gate home would typically need thirteen treads, thirteen risers, and matching nosing where the stairs land on the new field floor downstairs.

Sarasota's newer builds toward Palmer Ranch's later phases sometimes carry an open-tread design already, in which case our work is refinishing or re-staining rather than covering. For everything else, we cut treads off-site to the exact width of each step, because the city's older houses in particular were framed before anyone owned a laser level, and no two steps in a ninety-year-old staircase are identical width. The staircase stays walkable throughout the job; we finish one tread and riser pair before opening the next.
stair-treads/sarasota.cost_html:
A Laurel Park refinish-in-place job, sanding and re-staining thirteen existing heart-pine treads rather than replacing them, runs on our $95 hourly rate plus finish materials, typically $1,200-$1,900 for a full staircase over two days.

A full replacement is priced per tread: a Gulf Gate 1985 model with thirteen treads and thirteen risers in solid hardwood runs $130-$220 per tread ($1,690-$2,860) plus $25-$65 per riser ($325-$845), for a typical 2026 installed range of $2,015-$3,705. Swapping the same staircase to engineered hardwood brings tread cost down to $110-$180 each ($1,430-$2,340), for a total of $1,755-$3,185. See our stair tread cost guide for the full per-material table.

faqs.q: Do Sarasota's downtown condo towers have stairs that need treads?
faqs.a: Almost never. Nearly every downtown Sarasota tower unit is single-level and reached by elevator, so stair-tread work in the city is concentrated in the two-story houses around Laurel Park, Gulf Gate and The Meadows rather than the condo market.

faqs.q: Should I refinish or replace the original stairs in a Laurel Park bungalow?
faqs.a: If the treads are heart-pine or oak and the wood itself isn't cracked or rotted, refinishing in place usually costs less than replacement and keeps the original material that's part of a 1920s-1950s Laurel Park home's character.

faqs.q: How many treads does a typical Gulf Gate two-story home need replaced?
faqs.a: A standard 1970s-90s Gulf Gate or Meadows-area two-story model runs twelve to fourteen treads for an eight-foot ceiling stair run, which is the number we price against when we quote a full staircase replacement.
